summary.text: Bill Hagerty is the Republican U.S. Senator from Tennessee, seeking a second term. A Vanderbilt-trained lawyer, he worked in consulting and private equity, served in the George H.W. Bush administration, and was Tennessee's commissioner of economic and community development (2011-2014) and U.S. Ambassador to Japan (2017-2019). He was first elected to the Senate in 2020.

paragraphs.text: Born in Gallatin, Tennessee, and originally from Sumner County; he graduated from Madisonville North Hopkins High School in Kentucky and became an Eagle Scout.
Earned a bachelor's degree (1981) and a law degree (1984), both from Vanderbilt University.

Began his business career at Boston Consulting Group, including three years based in Tokyo, then worked in venture capital and private equity as an investor, executive and board member. According to Ballotpedia, he founded and was managing director of Hagerty Peterson & Company.
Worked in the George H. W. Bush administration on the domestic policy staff and as a White House Fellow, and served as national finance chair of Mitt Romney's 2008 presidential campaign.

From 2011 to 2014 he was Tennessee commissioner of economic and community development in Gov. Bill Haslam's cabinet; his official biography says he reorganized the department and cut over 40% of its positions.
Served on Donald Trump's 2016-2017 presidential transition team, where he oversaw presidential appointments.
Nominated by President Trump as U.S. Ambassador to Japan in March 2017, he was confirmed 86-12 on July 13, 2017. He announced in July 2019 that he would resign to run for the Senate.

Won the 2020 Republican primary for the open seat of retiring Sen. Lamar Alexander and defeated Democrat Marquita Bradshaw in the general election, 1,840,926 votes to 1,040,691. He took office January 3, 2021.

Serves on the Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs, Foreign Relations, Appropriations, and Rules and Administration committees. Wikipedia credits him with drafting the GENIUS Act, a stablecoin law signed July 18, 2025.
Was unopposed in the August 6, 2026 Republican primary (623,538 votes). According to his official biography, he and his wife Chrissy live in Davidson County and have four children.
